output:
Dear Mr Kehinde Ogunleye,

Thank you for picking up my black Jansport bag and making the effort to call the number on my lab manual. I am grateful that you kept it safe instead of leaving it behind or throwing it away.

I forgot the bag in the Oshodi-to-Igando danfo on Friday evening, 6 November, when I came down at Ikotun. It contains my lab manual, dissecting kit, student ID card, two textbooks, calculator and glasses. These are important things I need for school, especially as a first-year Biology student.

Sir, I am asking you to please reconsider the ₦40,000 you requested. I genuinely cannot afford it. I can manage ₦10,000 towards your transport and as a sincere thank-you for your help. That is my entire allowance, and it is the highest amount I can offer. I can give it to you when we meet and you return the bag.

My BIO 101 practical is on Wednesday, 11 November, at 10 a.m. Without my dissecting kit, I will not be allowed into the laboratory. Getting the bag back before then is therefore very important to me.

You spoke kindly during our first call, and I was relieved to hear from you. However, being told to pay ₦40,000 “or forget the bag” was upsetting. I appreciate your help, but I do not think it is fair to make returning my belongings depend on a payment I cannot afford.

Please choose a convenient daytime meeting before Wednesday. My roommate, Adaeze, will accompany me. We could meet at Ikotun roundabout or, if it is more convenient, outside the Ikotun Police Division gate—simply as an easy-to-find public meeting point.

Please reply to confirm a time and place, and kindly keep the bag and everything inside safe until then.

Thank you for your understanding.

Yours sincerely,  
[Your name]
